title: Perfect Born Sampling of Symmetric Thermal Tensor Network for Quantum Lattice Models
authors: Jianxin Gao, Qiaoyi Li, Yuan Gao, Chuanshu Xu, Guoliang Wu, Su Yi, Bin-Bin Chen, Wei Li
abstract: Accurate calculations of quantum lattice models at low temperatures constitute a major challenge in many-body physics. Stochastic sampling of tensor-network states offers a promising route to tackle this problem; however, existing schemes have long faced a fundamental dilemma---sampling efficiency and symmetry acceleration \textit{cannot} be achieved simultaneously. Here we propose a perfect Born sampling approach for thermal tensor networks, which performs importance sampling directly from the purified density matrix via the Born rule and incorporates Abelian and non-Abelian symmetries by sampling symmetry quantum numbers. We benchmark the method, realized as both stochastic matrix product states (stoMPS) and stochastic projected entangled pair states (stoPEPS), on large-scale quantum lattice models. Using stoMPS, we accurately simulate the square-lattice Hubbard model on cylinders up to width $W=10$, and study the triangular-lattice Hubbard model down to $T/t = 1/64$, revealing scalar chiral order at half filling and kinetic ferromagnetism upon electron doping. We further extend the stoMPS method to compute finite-temperature quantum dynamics, as demonstrated by the optical conductivity of the Hubbard model, and generalize it to stoPEPS, as showcased on the $20\times20$ square-lattice quantum Ising model at its quantum critical point. Our method combines high sampling efficiency with full symmetry acceleration, and can be used as a state-of-the-art framework for studying both equilibrium and dynamical properties down to ultralow temperatures.
summary: This paper introduces a novel perfect Born sampling technique for thermal tensor networks, designed to overcome the trade-off between sampling efficiency and symmetry enforcement in quantum simulations. By implementing this method using stoMPS and stoPEPS, the authors accurately simulate complex models like the Hubbard model at ultralow temperatures, revealing key magnetic and electronic phases.
main_problem: Accurately calculating quantum lattice models at low temperatures remains a major challenge in many-body physics.
main_result: The proposed method successfully combines high sampling efficiency with full symmetry acceleration, allowing for state-of-the-art study of both equilibrium and dynamical properties down to ultralow temperatures.
method: The authors propose a perfect Born sampling approach for thermal tensor networks, which performs importance sampling directly from the purified density matrix while incorporating Abelian and non-Abelian symmetries by sampling symmetry quantum numbers.
model_or_system: The method is benchmarked on quantum lattice models, including the Hubbard model (on square and triangular lattices) and the quantum Ising model. It is implemented using stochastic matrix product states (stoMPS) and stochastic projected entangled pair states (stoPEPS).
key_observables: Energy per site, thermal expectation values of observables (e.g., optical conductivity), and detection of magnetic orders like scalar chiral order and kinetic ferromagnetism.
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($T/t$ down to $1/64$), system widths up to $W=10$, and quantum critical points.
main_assumptions: Existing stochastic schemes face a fundamental dilemma where sampling efficiency and symmetry acceleration cannot be achieved simultaneously.
figures_summary: Figure 1 diagrammatically illustrates the stoMPS method, showing Born sampling via projection of the purified supervector. Other figures compare energy per site estimates from the method against established benchmarks like DQMC.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the core concept of perfect Born sampling for thermal tensor networks, details its implementation via stoMPS and stoPEPS, and then presents benchmarks on the Hubbard and Ising models to validate its accuracy and efficiency for both equilibrium and dynamic properties.
why_interesting: The combination of advanced tensor network techniques (MPS/PEPS) with rigorous sampling methods (Born rule) to handle symmetries and low temperatures makes it a powerful tool for simulating complex quantum dynamics relevant to strongly correlated materials.
